To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
freshmen students reported a significantly lower level of vocational purpose than seniors.
there were significant differences between seniors and freshmen on the development of vocation in college.
freshmen and seniors significantly differ in their development of purpose in college.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sixth vector, "developing purpose," in college students' development.
the development of vocational purposes in college.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

students who are more involved in campus life, who have a more positive perception of their college experience, who have more positive perceptions of their college major, who are more satisfied with their major, and who perceive themselves as more prepared to enter their chosen profession will have a higher level of purpose development in college than students who do not.
the results of this study indicate that the development of vocational purposes in college is a significant factor in the development of the whole person.
the present study has provided some empirical support for the notion that college seniors are more purposeful and have a clearer idea about the direction of their lives than college freshmen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found that students do develop vocational purpose in college, and that there are significant differences between freshmen and seniors in their development of vocational purpose, as measured by the IVPI (Iowa Vocational Purpose Inventory).
the development of purpose in college is not a linear process.
students who are in their senior year of college have developed a greater sense of purpose than students in their freshman year.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the college experience is a critical period for developing vocational purpose, and that this development is not a simple linear process.

students are more likely to be purposeful when they are able to identify their interests, abilities, and skills and when they are able, with the help of their parents and teachers, to make connections between those things and potential careers.
the development of a sense of purpose in college is a process that unfolds over the course of the college years.
